questions.question: ___ Mann ist sehr nett.
questions.explanation: Mann is masculine, so the definite article is Der.

questions.question: ___ Frau kommt aus Berlin.
questions.explanation: Frau is feminine, so the definite article is Die.

questions.question: ___ Kind spielt im Garten.
questions.translation: The child is playing in the garden.
questions.explanation: Kind is neuter, so the definite article is Das.

questions.question: ___ Bücher sind interessant.
questions.explanation: Die is used as the definite article for plural nouns.

questions.question: Das ist ___ Apfel.
questions.explanation: Apfel is masculine. Ein is used for masculine nouns in the nominative case.

questions.question: Ich habe ___ Katze.
questions.explanation: Katze is feminine. Eine is used for feminine nouns in the accusative case.

questions.question: Er kauft ___ Auto.
questions.explanation: Auto is neuter. Ein remains Ein in the accusative case.

questions.question: Das ist ___ Lehrerin.
questions.explanation: Lehrerin is feminine, so the indefinite article is Eine.

questions.question: Ich sehe ___ Hund.
questions.explanation: Hund is masculine and is the direct object. Der changes to Den in the accusative case.

questions.question: Sie liest ___ Zeitung.
questions.explanation: Zeitung is feminine. Die remains Die in the accusative case.

questions.question: Ich ___ Deutsch.
questions.explanation: The verb lernen takes the ending -e with ich.

questions.question: Du ___ Fußball.
questions.explanation: Regular verbs take the ending -st with du.

questions.question: Er ___ jeden Tag Kaffee.
questions.explanation: Trinken takes the ending -t with er.

questions.question: Wir ___ in Berlin.
questions.explanation: The verb wohnen takes the ending -en with wir.

questions.question: Ihr ___ sehr schnell.
questions.explanation: The verb laufen takes the ending -t with ihr.

questions.question: Sie (formal) ___ Englisch.
questions.explanation: Formal Sie uses the infinitive form ending -en.

questions.question: Meine Mutter ___ heute.
questions.explanation: Meine Mutter is third-person singular, so arbeiten becomes arbeitet.

questions.question: Ihr ___ Musik.
questions.explanation: The verb hören takes the ending -t with ihr.

questions.question: Ich ___ müde.
questions.explanation: The verb sein is irregular. Its ich form is bin.

questions.question: Du ___ sehr nett.
questions.explanation: The verb sein takes the form bist with du.

questions.question: Maria ist meine Schwester. ___ ist nett.
questions.translation: Maria is my sister. She is nice.
questions.explanation: Sie is the personal pronoun for a feminine person.

questions.question: Peter ist mein Bruder. ___ ist 20 Jahre alt.
questions.translation: Peter is my brother. He is 20 years old.
questions.explanation: Er is the personal pronoun for a masculine person.

questions.question: Das Baby schläft. ___ ist müde.
questions.translation: The baby is sleeping. It is tired.
questions.explanation: Das Baby is grammatically neuter, so the pronoun is Es.

questions.question: Tom und ich spielen Fußball. ___ sind Freunde.
questions.translation: Tom and I play football. We are friends.
questions.explanation: Wir means we and refers to Tom and the speaker.

questions.question: Anna und Lisa sind hier. ___ lernen Deutsch.
questions.translation: Anna and Lisa are here. They learn German.
questions.explanation: Sie means they when referring to multiple people.

questions.question: Paul, ___ bist mein Freund.
questions.explanation: Du is the informal singular pronoun for you.

questions.question: Herr Müller, ___ sind sehr freundlich.
questions.translation: Mr. Müller, you are very friendly.
questions.explanation: Formal Sie is used to address someone politely.

questions.question: Kinder, ___ seid sehr laut!
questions.explanation: Ihr is the informal plural pronoun for you.

questions.question: Meine Eltern sind zu Hause. ___ kochen.
questions.translation: My parents are at home. They are cooking.
questions.explanation: Sie means they when referring to multiple people.

questions.question: Ich und mein Bruder lernen. ___ lernen zusammen.
questions.translation: My brother and I study. We study together.
questions.explanation: Wir means we and refers to the speaker and another person.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: In a basic German statement, the conjugated verb usually comes in the second position.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: The subject comes first and the conjugated verb comes second in a basic statement.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: Heute ___ ich Deutsch.
questions.explanation: When Heute comes first, the conjugated verb must come second, before the subject.

questions.question: Choose the correct question.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question in German starts with the conjugated verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: When Heute is first, gehen comes second and the subject follows.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: Wo ___ du?
questions.explanation: With du, the verb wohnen becomes wohnst.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: The conjugated verb comes second, and the masculine direct object uses einen.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Morgen occupies the first position, so the verb besuchen comes second.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: Ich ___ heute zu Hause.
questions.explanation: The correct form of sein with ich is bin.

questions.question: Choose the correct question.
questions.explanation: In a question beginning with Wo, the conjugated verb follows the question word.

questions.question: Ich ___ jeden Morgen Kaffee.
questions.explanation: Trinken is conjugated as trinke with ich.

questions.question: Du ___ sehr gut Deutsch.
questions.explanation: Sprechen is a stem-changing verb. With du, e changes to i and the ending is -st.

questions.question: Meine Schwester ___ gern Musik.
questions.translation: My sister likes listening to music.
questions.explanation: Meine Schwester is third-person singular, so hören becomes hört.

questions.question: Wir ___ heute Pizza.
questions.explanation: The verb essen takes the form essen with wir.

questions.question: Ihr ___ heute Fußball.
questions.explanation: With ihr, the regular verb spielen takes the ending -t.

questions.question: Er ___ ein Buch.
questions.explanation: Lesen is a stem-changing verb. With er, e changes to ie.

questions.question: Ich ___ einen Bruder.
questions.explanation: The verb haben takes the form habe with ich.

questions.question: Du ___ ein neues Handy.
questions.translation: You have a new mobile phone.
questions.explanation: The verb haben takes the form hast with du.

questions.question: Das Kind ___ Wasser.
questions.explanation: Das Kind is third-person singular, so trinken becomes trinkt.

questions.question: Meine Freunde ___ in München.
questions.explanation: Meine Freunde is plural, so wohnen takes the ending -en.

questions.question: Ich ___ aus Indien.
questions.explanation: Kommen takes the ending -e with ich.

questions.question: Woher ___ ihr?
questions.translation: Where do you all come from?
questions.explanation: The verb kommen takes the form kommt with ihr.

questions.question: Sie (they) ___ in einem Haus.
questions.explanation: Plural Sie meaning they uses the verb form wohnen.

questions.question: Der Vater ___ ein Auto.
questions.explanation: Fahren is a stem-changing verb. With er, a changes to ä.

questions.question: Du ___ gern Schokolade.
questions.explanation: Essen is a stem-changing verb. With du, the correct form is isst.

questions.question: Wir ___ einen Film.
questions.explanation: The verb sehen takes the form sehen with wir.

questions.question: ___ Mädchen spielt mit einem Ball.
questions.translation: The girl is playing with a ball.
questions.explanation: Mädchen is grammatically neuter, so its definite article is Das.

questions.question: Ich kaufe ___ Banane.
questions.explanation: Banane is feminine, so the accusative indefinite article is Eine.

questions.question: ___ Lehrer arbeitet heute.
questions.explanation: Lehrer is masculine and is the subject, so the article is Der.

questions.question: Das ist ___ Buch.
questions.explanation: Buch is neuter, so the indefinite article is Ein.

questions.question: Lisa und du seid Freunde. ___ lernt Deutsch.
questions.translation: Lisa and you are friends. You are learning German.
questions.explanation: Ihr is used when speaking informally to two or more people.

questions.question: Das Auto ist neu. ___ ist rot.
questions.translation: The car is new. It is red.
questions.explanation: Das Auto is neuter, so the correct pronoun is Es.

questions.question: Ich ___ heute nicht zur Schule.
questions.translation: I am not going to school today.
questions.explanation: The verb gehen takes the form gehe with ich.

questions.question: Er ___ um sieben Uhr auf.
questions.translation: He gets up at seven o'clock.
questions.explanation: Aufstehen is a separable verb. With er, it becomes steht ... auf.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: The conjugated verb esse occupies the second position in the statement.

questions.question: Complete the question: Wann ___ du nach Hause?
questions.explanation: With du, the verb gehen becomes gehst.

questions.question: Meine Eltern ___ sehr freundlich.
questions.explanation: The verb sein takes the form sind with plural subjects.

questions.question: Du ___ deine Hausaufgaben.
questions.explanation: Machen takes the ending -st with du.

questions.question: Der Junge ___ schnell.
questions.explanation: Laufen is a stem-changing verb. With er, au changes to äu.

questions.question: Er braucht ___ Stuhl.
questions.explanation: Stuhl is masculine and is the direct object. Ein changes to Einen in the accusative case.
